$comment: Disposition registry for test-book-e2e.md cases that browser collection alone cannot express. It never maps a case to a test: mappings come from collected Playwright titles/annotations and executed node --test titles. `owners` name the suite whose own contract test must hold a marked test (middleware: @pytest.mark.book; embedder: @book_case). `exclusions` need a written reason of at least 40 characters and fail the gate as soon as the case gains evidence. `ratchet.maxUnassigned` may only be lowered.

exclusions.reason: Series Z is the book's manual BASIC<->ADVANCED operator roundtrip (§12: 'an operator workflow, not an automated roundtrip'). Z1 is the BASIC-side create/index/seed/query step whose automated equivalents are the live Collections/Ingest/Query suites and TB-PRO-001 (external config). It is recorded per operator run in the §16.7 addendum, never mapped to a default-run test.

Series Z operator step performed after a real profile switch to ADVANCED (create/seed/query while the BASIC-born collection stays locked). Requires a service restart with SMART_EMBEDDER_PROFILE=advanced; observed only through the external configuration (TB-PRO-001/z4-switch) and recorded per operator run.

Series Z operator step: a second real profile switch back to BASIC and re-test of both collections. Needs two service restarts in one run; the runner cannot create that state. Covered procedurally by TB-PRO-001 under the external configuration and recorded per operator run.

Series Z cleanup step (delete e2e_a_new*, e2e_a_victim, e2e_a_empty; keep protected fixtures). It is an operator housekeeping action on the manual roundtrip; automated runs clean their own owned targets through the campaign manifest (TB-HAR-001/002) instead.

Four-cell hardware/profile matrix (CPU/GPU x BASIC/ADVANCED). Each cell is a separate stack start on specific hardware; cells without the hardware are BLOCKED with reason per the book, never mocked. Recorded as operator evidence in §16.7; no single-run test can claim it.

API-live performance benchmark (input length x concurrency cells, warmups, measured batches, RAM/VRAM sampling on fixed hardware) that the book itself schedules 'after admission policy exists'. It is an operator benchmark campaign, not a pass/fail suite the runner can execute; results are recorded per hardware cell in §16.7. TB-PER-001 (embedder unittest) owns the admission-budget contract.
